phases.name: Define the trading and evidence boundaries
phases.description: Treat the prompt metrics as evaluation gates and separate offline experimentation, paper trading, and live execution.

phases.name: Build historical and simulated environments
phases.description: Preserve point-in-time market data and simulate execution frictions before training an agent.

phases.name: Train, evaluate, and register policies
phases.description: Make reward, walk-forward evaluation, regime features, and model provenance explicit.

phases.name: Separate inference, risk, and execution
phases.description: Keep the low-latency path bounded, enforce risk independently of the policy, and make paper results auditable.

phases.name: Capacity and launch review
phases.description: Benchmark the stated instrument and latency targets; no backtest score is a live performance guarantee.

steps.phase: Define the trading and evidence boundaries
steps.title: Read the frozen trading brief
steps.content: Design a Reinforcement Learning Trading System. Design a reinforcement learning-based trading system that learns optimal trading strategies from market data, manages risk, and executes trades with low latency while adapting to market regime changes. Functional requirements: Train RL agents on historical market data; Define reward functions balancing returns and risk; Handle continuous action spaces for position sizing; Implement market environment simulation; Support multiple asset classes; Implement risk management constraints; Detect and adapt to market regime changes; Provide backtesting and paper trading capabilities. Non-functional constraints: Sharpe ratio above 1.5 in backtests; Maximum drawdown below 15%; Trade execution latency under 10ms; Handle 1000+ instruments simultaneously; Avoid overfitting to historical data. Hints: Use PPO or SAC algorithms for continuous action spaces; Implement realistic market simulators with slippage and fees; Use multi-agent RL for portfolio optimization; Implement walk-forward validation to prevent overfitting; Use attention mechanisms for market state representation; Implement regime detection with Hidden Markov Models. These are supplied targets and suggestions, not evidence of live profitability or safe execution.

steps.phase: Define the trading and evidence boundaries
steps.title: Clarify what the prompt leaves open
steps.content: Ask which venues, asset classes, trading hours, bar/tick frequencies, order types, fee schedules, slippage model, financing/borrow costs, market-impact assumptions, capital limits, and latency measurement boundary apply. Define Sharpe frequency and annualization, drawdown calculation, out-of-sample windows, instrument universe/survivorship rules, and whether the 10ms clock starts at signal generation or at venue acknowledgement. Do not invent these values or interpret a backtest as a guarantee.

steps.phase: Define the trading and evidence boundaries
steps.title: Keep research, paper, and live paths isolated
steps.content: The same versioned policy can be evaluated in a simulator and in paper mode, but simulated orders must never enter the live execution route. The 10ms execution target belongs to a deliberately short hot path, not the historical data or training pipeline.

decision.question: Should historical replay, model training, and live orders share one synchronous pipeline?
decision.chosen: Use separate offline research and online execution paths with a strict, independently enforced risk boundary.
decision.chosenReason: This prevents training/replay load from adding unpredictable work to execution and prevents paper orders from reaching a live venue.

alternatives.option: Run training or replay in the live request path
alternatives.tradeoff: Unbounded compute and I/O make latency and operational isolation difficult.

alternatives.option: Let the policy send orders directly to the venue
alternatives.tradeoff: A model defect can bypass deterministic exposure, freshness, and kill-switch controls.

steps.title: Normalize market data across asset classes
steps.content: The catalog has no exchange-feed component, so use a custom adapter for venue-specific protocols. Normalize instrument identity, event time, sequence, currency, corporate actions, and source quality without assuming a common session calendar.

component.label: Market Data Adapters
component.description: Normalizes live and historical market events across configured asset classes.

properties.purpose: Normalize configured asset-class and venue feeds with instrument identity, event time, sequence, currency, session, and source-quality metadata.

component.highlightReason: Multiple asset classes are explicit; their protocols, calendars, and data entitlements must be isolated behind adapters.

steps.title: Decouple market capture from research consumers
steps.content: Use a partitioned event stream for capture, replay, and asynchronous consumers. Do not put this broker on the latency-critical order path unless measurements prove the chosen topology meets the 10ms target.

component.label: Market Event Archive Stream
component.description: Durable asynchronous transport for replay and research data.

properties.purpose: Buffer normalized market events for archival and offline research; partition by a stable instrument key and size retention from measured event rates.

component.highlightReason: Historical replay and model training need a durable feed but must remain off the live execution hot path.

steps.title: Publish a replayable market event record
steps.content: Retain source sequence and event time so replay can detect gaps and ordering defects. Entitlement and redistribution rules belong at the adapter boundary.

connection.label: Normalized market events
connection.description: Asynchronous event capture with source, instrument, event-time, sequence, and quality metadata.

steps.title: Version the historical research dataset
steps.content: Store immutable or versioned source partitions and corporate-action/metadata snapshots. Training and backtests must use only data available at the simulated decision time; corrections create new dataset versions rather than silently rewriting results.

component.label: Point-in-Time Market History
component.description: Versioned event history for simulation, training, and audit.

properties.purpose: Retain versioned market events, instrument metadata, corporate actions, and dataset manifests for point-in-time replay and reproducible evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Leakage and survivorship bias often enter through data revisions and universe construction, not only model code.

steps.title: Archive asynchronously from the capture stream
steps.content: Keep archival independent of live decisions. Verify completeness with sequence-gap checks and immutable manifests before data is admitted to a backtest.

connection.label: Versioned market partitions
connection.description: Durable asynchronous market history with capture manifests and source quality metadata.

steps.title: Model the market and execution mechanics
steps.content: Build a simulator that accounts for fees, spread, slippage, partial fills, market hours, and a defensible market-impact model. The simulator is a custom domain component because no catalog item models a point-in-time trading environment.

component.label: Market and Execution Simulator
component.description: Runs point-in-time backtests and isolated paper-trading sessions.

properties.purpose: Replay point-in-time market state and model fees, slippage, order types, partial fills, sessions, and documented market-impact assumptions for backtesting and paper trading.

component.highlightReason: Realistic simulation is required to evaluate reward and risk; friction assumptions materially change measured Sharpe and drawdown.

steps.title: Replay only data available at each decision time
steps.content: Construct point-in-time bars/state with no future prices, revised fundamentals, or surviving-only universe leakage. Keep simulator version and friction configuration in the experiment record.

connection.label: Point-in-time market replay
connection.description: Immutable market and instrument snapshots presented only as they would have been known at each simulated time.

steps.title: Train policy candidates inside the environment
steps.content: Compare PPO or SAC candidates against simple baselines across multiple seeds and temporal folds. Record action bounds, observation versions, reward version, training code, and all data/simulator manifests.

component.label: RL Policy Training
component.description: Trains and compares agents against the versioned simulated market.

properties.purpose: Train reinforcement-learning candidates such as PPO or SAC inside the versioned environment; record observation, action, reward, seed, dataset, and simulator versions.

component.highlightReason: Historical training must be coupled to an explicit environment and reward, not directly to live execution.

steps.title: Use simulated transitions for policy learning
steps.content: Store transition provenance and separate training from evaluation folds. Avoid evaluating on the same episodes used to tune reward coefficients or select checkpoints.

connection.label: Simulated transitions and rewards
connection.description: Versioned observations, actions, fills, costs, portfolio state, and terminal outcomes for training.

steps.title: Track every policy and experiment version
steps.content: Register policy weights with reward, environment, feature, data, code, seed, and evaluation manifests. Retain rejected candidates too, so selection decisions and backtests can be reproduced.

component.label: Trading Policy Registry
component.description: Versions policy artifacts, experiment metadata, and evaluation evidence.

properties.purpose: Version policy artifacts and bind them to data, reward, simulator, code, feature, and evaluation manifests for reproducibility and rollback.

component.highlightReason: Changing reward or simulator assumptions changes the policy's meaning and requires traceable versions.

steps.title: Evaluate on walk-forward windows and realistic costs
steps.content: Use a custom gate for multiple walk-forward windows, untouched holdouts, multiple seeds, realistic cost sensitivity, and regime slices. The Sharpe >1.5 and drawdown <15% values are supplied targets; define calculation conventions and confidence before promotion.

component.label: Walk-Forward Risk Evaluation
component.description: Tests strategy robustness and prompt acceptance metrics before promotion.

properties.technology: Temporal folds and cost stress tests
properties.purpose: Measure Sharpe and maximum drawdown on untouched walk-forward periods, multiple seeds, asset-class/regime slices, and cost-stressed simulations; block promotion when the agreed protocol is not met.

component.highlightReason: A high backtest score can be an artifact of leakage, tuning, or unrealistic fills; the prompt requires explicit overfit controls.

steps.title: Gate against data not used for tuning
steps.content: Keep walk-forward boundaries and evaluation code immutable for a candidate run. Include slippage/fee sensitivity and compare with non-RL baselines before accepting a policy.

connection.label: Policy candidates and fold results
connection.description: Frozen candidates, temporal split manifests, seeds, costs, and per-window risk/return metrics.

steps.title: Register only evidence-backed candidates
steps.content: Attach exact metric definitions, fold outcomes, and approvals to a registered policy. Do not collapse a distribution of window results into one unqualified headline number.

connection.label: Qualified policy and report
connection.description: A versioned candidate plus walk-forward evidence and an explicit promotion decision.

steps.title: Model the continuous position-sizing policy
steps.content: Represent the policy's continuous outputs as bounded target positions or deltas. Convert them to valid orders only after deterministic exposure, cash, leverage, freshness, and venue checks; the prompt supplies no numeric risk limits.

component.label: Continuous-Action Trading Policy
component.description: Maps the approved market state to continuous position-sizing actions.

properties.purpose: Produce bounded continuous target-position proposals from the documented observation and reward versions; proposals are not executable orders until the independent risk service approves them.

component.highlightReason: Continuous action spaces are explicitly required, but a model output must be projected into allowed orders and risk limits.

steps.title: Pin the exact policy artifact
steps.content: Deploy by immutable digest and retain a fast rollback to a previously approved version. Keep policy metadata and runtime observation schema compatible before activation.

connection.label: Approved policy artifact
connection.description: Immutable policy version with reward, data, environment, and evaluation provenance.

steps.title: Detect market regimes as versioned context
steps.content: A regime detector can use an HMM or another validated method, but regimes are uncertain estimates rather than known labels. Evaluate stability, delay, and false transitions across assets and time.

component.label: Market Regime Detector
component.description: Estimates regime context for policy conditioning and evaluation.

properties.purpose: Estimate versioned market-regime context from point-in-time observations and expose confidence and transition behavior for policy conditioning and evaluation.

component.highlightReason: The brief requires adaptation to regime changes, but does not define regimes or label quality.

steps.title: Version regime logic with the policy
steps.content: Record the detector version and regime-state schema with each policy. Backtests must compute regime state using only data observable at that time.

connection.label: Approved regime artifact
connection.description: Versioned regime estimator, confidence behavior, and point-in-time input contract.

steps.title: Make reward trade-offs inspectable
steps.content: Define a reward that balances returns and risk and accounts for turnover and execution costs. If drawdown limits are hard constraints, enforce them in the risk system as well as evaluate them offline; a reward penalty alone cannot guarantee a maximum drawdown.

steps.title: Serve an approved policy on the hot path
steps.content: Load pinned policy and regime versions and keep inference work bounded. The under-10ms target is a measured end-to-end budget; this catalog component does not guarantee it, and the boundary must be agreed with the venue.

component.label: Low-Latency Policy Inference
component.description: Produces position proposals from fresh market state and approved model versions.

properties.purpose: Run approved policy and regime artifacts on bounded, fresh observations and return target-position proposals with model version and inference timing.

component.highlightReason: Inference belongs on the online path; model loading, cold starts, and feature access must be included in latency measurement.

steps.title: Load the approved continuous-action policy
steps.content: Validate the action schema and reject incompatible policy versions before a rollout. A model promotion should be atomic from the serving process's perspective.

connection.label: Pinned policy and action schema
connection.description: Approved continuous-action artifact and its observation/action contract.

steps.title: Condition inference on current regime evidence
steps.content: Pass regime estimate, confidence, and timestamp as explicit context. Define conservative behavior for missing, stale, or low-confidence regime state.

connection.label: Regime estimate and confidence
connection.description: Versioned point-in-time regime context for policy conditioning.

steps.title: Feed live observations directly to inference
steps.content: Keep the market-event archive broker off this direct live observation route. Measure market-event age and inference time separately, then measure the agreed complete signal-to-execution interval.

connection.label: Fresh market observations
connection.description: Bounded live market state delivered directly to inference, outside the asynchronous archival path.

steps.title: Keep approved portfolio state close to risk checks
steps.content: Cache can reduce repeated reads for read-mostly state, but never make it the sole authority for balances, exposure, or order idempotency. Include version/freshness and fail closed if authoritative state cannot be confirmed.

component.label: Market and Portfolio Snapshot Cache
component.description: Low-latency, versioned read cache for bounded decision context.

properties.purpose: Cache versioned market and portfolio snapshots for risk evaluation while preserving the ledger as authoritative state and rejecting stale snapshots.

component.highlightReason: The stated low-latency target encourages fast reads, but risk decisions cannot depend on stale cached exposure.

steps.title: Enforce deterministic risk independently
steps.content: Apply owner-approved limits for exposure, cash, leverage, instrument eligibility, order size, stale data, and kill switches. The prompt requires risk constraints but supplies no numeric limits; reject or hold proposals when authoritative state is unavailable.

component.label: Pre-Trade Risk and Order Policy
component.description: Validates every model proposal against deterministic account and venue rules.

properties.purpose: Validate target-position proposals, fresh state, instrument eligibility, owner-defined exposure limits, order bounds, idempotency, and kill-switch state; fail closed on uncertain risk state.

component.highlightReason: A learned reward does not replace deterministic risk controls or an independently operable kill switch.

steps.title: Read versioned context without trusting stale values
steps.content: Risk checks validate snapshot age/version against explicit policy and consult the authoritative ledger when required. Missing or stale account state must stop order submission.

connection.label: Versioned risk context
connection.description: Read-optimized snapshot with timestamp and version, subject to freshness validation.

steps.title: Submit proposals, not executable orders
steps.content: Attach policy version, observation timestamp, instrument, target position, confidence/diagnostics, and correlation ID. Risk owns the final conversion to an order.

connection.label: Position proposal
connection.description: Bounded model output and provenance for deterministic pre-trade validation.

steps.title: Isolate venue execution behind an adapter
steps.content: Translate approved orders to venue protocols, enforce idempotency, reconcile acknowledgements/fills, and report timeouts without blind duplicate submission. Keep credentials and venue-specific rules outside the policy model.

component.label: Broker and Venue Execution Adapter
component.description: Submits risk-approved orders and reconciles venue responses.

properties.purpose: Submit only risk-approved orders with idempotency and correlation IDs, enforce venue protocol rules, and reconcile acknowledgement, partial fill, rejection, and timeout states.

component.highlightReason: Execution latency and order correctness need an explicit venue boundary and auditable state transitions.

steps.title: Send only approved orders to a venue
steps.content: Measure risk-check and venue acknowledgement latency separately as well as the end-to-end metric. Persist idempotency state before retrying ambiguous timeouts.

connection.label: Approved order intent
connection.description: Risk-approved, bounded, idempotent order request with instrument and policy provenance.

steps.title: Maintain an authoritative order and portfolio ledger
steps.content: Record proposals, approvals/rejections, order state transitions, fills, positions, cash, and reconciliations with immutable correlation and policy identifiers. Define transactional consistency and recovery before live use.

component.label: Orders and Portfolio Ledger
component.description: Authoritative record for approved orders, fills, and account state.

properties.purpose: Persist idempotent order intents, acknowledgements, fills, positions, cash, approvals, and reconciliation history as authoritative risk state.

component.highlightReason: Risk checks require trustworthy positions and every execution outcome must be auditable.

steps.title: Reconcile venue outcomes into the ledger
steps.content: Process venue callbacks idempotently and reconcile open/partial/filled/rejected states. A timeout is an unknown outcome until queried, not proof that an order failed.

connection.label: Order and fill reconciliation
connection.description: Durable venue acknowledgements, fill events, order state, and resulting position updates.

steps.title: Keep research controls off direct venue credentials
steps.content: Expose authenticated, audited controls for experiment launch, approved paper sessions, and read-only results. Separate permissions for research, approval, and any later live activation.

component.label: Research and Paper-Trading API
component.description: Authenticated control plane for simulation requests and result retrieval.

properties.purpose: Authorize and audit backtest and isolated paper-session requests, validate experiment inputs, and expose results without exposing live venue credentials.

component.highlightReason: Backtesting and paper trading are explicit user capabilities; control-plane access must not bypass live risk and execution boundaries.

steps.title: Provide an auditable research surface
steps.content: Show dataset and simulator versions, split boundaries, costs, reward definition, policy digest, fold metrics, drawdown, and paper/live state. Make it visually impossible to confuse simulated fills with actual venue fills.

component.label: Strategy Research Console
component.description: Compares reproducible backtests and isolated paper sessions.

properties.purpose: Launch authorized research and paper sessions and review dataset, simulator, policy, costs, fold results, risk metrics, and clear paper-versus-live status.

component.highlightReason: Researchers need reproducible comparisons without treating a single backtest number as live evidence.

steps.title: Authenticate experiment and paper-session requests
steps.content: Use scoped authorization and immutable request IDs; paper-session controls must never grant live venue privileges.

connection.label: Research and paper controls
connection.description: Authenticated, audited API calls to create simulations and retrieve evaluation results.

steps.title: Run backtests and paper sessions in isolation
steps.content: The simulator owns isolated paper state and realistic execution frictions. Paper orders and simulated fills must not share the live venue adapter's route or credentials.

connection.label: Versioned simulation request
connection.description: Authorized backtest or paper-session command with frozen policy, market, reward, and simulator versions.

steps.title: Persist paper outcomes with explicit mode
steps.content: Use a separate paper account namespace and label every simulated order/fill as paper. The simulator must not be able to reach the live execution adapter.

connection.label: Isolated paper results
connection.description: Paper-mode proposals and simulated fills stored with a distinct account and environment identity.

steps.title: Observe live risk and model behavior
steps.content: Track market-data freshness, policy/regime versions, inference and risk latency, rejected proposals, venue acknowledgements, exposure, drawdown, and kill-switch state. Monitoring alerts do not replace an independently operable stop control.

component.label: Trading Risk and Latency Monitoring
component.description: Observes model, risk, venue, and portfolio behavior.

properties.purpose: Measure market-state age, inference and execution latency, policy versions, risk rejects, venue state, exposure, drawdown, and operational kill-switch status.

component.highlightReason: Low-latency execution and risk constraints require live measurement and operational response.

steps.title: Measure the inference portion of the budget
steps.content: Record warm/cold inference separately and include feature acquisition and serialization. The 10ms execution target's start/end boundary still needs product and venue agreement.

connection.label: Inference timing and version
connection.description: Policy latency, model identity, input freshness, and error telemetry.

steps.title: Measure venue outcomes and risk state
steps.content: Measure submission-to-acknowledgement and fill latency, plus risk-check time and order-state reconciliation. Alert on stale position state and stop new orders when the safe state cannot be established.

connection.label: Venue and risk telemetry
connection.description: Order acknowledgement/fill timing, rejects, reconciliation state, and risk-control signals.

steps.title: Benchmark the 1000-instrument target
steps.content: The prompt gives an instrument count but no tick rate, asset mix, or portfolio cardinality. Load-test correlated bursts, market open/close behavior, model state size, and recovery; avoid inventing a qps or partition count.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-instrument event age, inference/risk/execution latency, queue depth, and concurrent active instruments
scaleTrigger.action: Partition independent research/archival workloads and add hot-path capacity only after profiling the measured bottleneck; preserve deterministic ordering and account-risk state.
scaleTrigger.impact: Validate simultaneous handling of 1000+ instruments and the agreed under-10ms boundary without allowing offline research to contend with live order processing.

steps.title: Decide what the metrics actually mean
steps.content: Agree the metric convention and test protocol before judging a candidate. The thresholds in the brief are goals to demonstrate under that protocol, not guarantees supplied by a component selection.

decision.question: Can one backtest Sharpe and drawdown result qualify a strategy for live orders?
decision.chosen: No; require frozen walk-forward evidence, costs and regime slices, paper results, independent risk approval, and measured latency before any live activation.
decision.chosenReason: Single-window backtests are vulnerable to tuning, data leakage, survivorship, and unrealistic execution assumptions.

alternatives.option: Promote the best historical Sharpe immediately
alternatives.tradeoff: Selection bias and unmodeled frictions can make apparent performance non-representative.

alternatives.option: Treat simulated latency as venue latency
alternatives.tradeoff: It omits network, risk, acknowledgement, and fill behavior outside the simulator.

steps.title: Keep limits and launch authority explicit
steps.content: Before any live use, obtain owner-approved exposure and loss limits, venue access controls, kill-switch ownership, reconciliation procedures, market-data licensing, and incident playbooks. The walkthrough describes an architecture for evaluating a strategy; it does not assert profitability, regulatory approval, or readiness for real-money execution.
